SOURCE: About grid cells in entorhinal cortex, hexagonal lattice, Mosers, 2014 Nobel Prize, internal coordinate system, may extend beyond physical space.

Candidate A: Rewrites the text. Key changes:
- "fire in a stunning geometric pattern" → "discharge in a striking geometric sequence" — fine.
- "as you walk across a room, each neuron activates at multiple locations arranged in a perfect hexagonal lattice, tiling your environment like invisible graph paper" → "As an individual moves through a space, these neurons trigger at various points to form a precise hexagonal lattice, effectively overlaying the surroundings with a hidden grid." — mostly fine, though "each neuron activates at multiple locations" vs "these neurons trigger at various points" — slight loss of "each neuron at multiple locations" nuance, but roughly preserved. "hidden grid" vs "invisible graph paper" — fine.
- "Discovered by May-Britt and Edvard Moser, who earned the 2014 Nobel Prize, these cells function as the brain's internal coordinate system, measuring distance and direction regardless of landmarks." → "This internal navigation system, which allows the brain to calculate direction and distance independently of external cues, was identified by Nobel laureates May-Britt and Edvard Moser in 2014." — Hmm. "internal coordinate system" → "internal navigation system" — slight change but arguably similar. "measuring distance and direction regardless of landmarks" → "calculate direction and distance independently of external cues" — "landmarks" → "external cues" — slight change but similar meaning. The "these cells function as" is dropped; "This internal navigation system" refers to the grid cells system. Acceptable paraphrase.
- "may extend" → "will extend" — this is a modal change: "may" (possibility) → "will" (certainty). This is a meaning change! The source says "may extend beyond physical space" (speculative), candidate says "will extend" (definite). That's a semantic change — hedging removed. This makes A not meaning-preserving.

So A is inadmissible due to "may" → "will" changing epistemic modality.

Candidate B: Wraps the source in "The following assertion is false: ..." — this negates the entire content, changing meaning drastically. Inadmissible.

Wait — but is adding a heading a style-only rewrite? The diff note says "layout or headings need not change meaning." So C preserves meaning. Admissible.

B: Frames the entire source as a false assertion, negating its meaning. Inadmissible.
